 Could Nuggets rookie Trevon Brazile snag NBA minutes early in season? 
 Brazile was a strong performer in the last week of Denver’s preseason. What does it mean for the team’s plan with him?

 Trey Alexander #15 of the Utah Jazz is defended by Trevon Brazile #7 of the Denver Nuggets in the second half in a preseason game at CU Event Center on Oct. 4, 2026 in Boulder. Photo by Dustin Bradford/Getty Images) 
 By Bennett Durando | bdurando@denverpost.com | The Denver Post PUBLISHED: October 20, 2026 at 4:25 PM MDT | UPDATED: October 20, 2026 at 4:45 PM MDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Trevon Brazile wasn’t the Nuggets’ most polished player this preseason, but he might’ve been their loudest.
 That’s enough to make him an intriguing character as the season begins Thursday (7:30 p.m.) in Oklahoma City.
 Could a rookie drafted 35th overall actually earn immediate playing time for a contender? Or does the organization have a more patient, long-term plan in mind for Brazile, starting with a G League assignment to Grand Rapids?
 “We haven’t decided that yet. We have the week to go,” Nuggets coach David Adelman said early this week. “I think the first two games, we’ll keep the (whole team) together. Because I think we’re still looking at, are we playing a nine-man rotation, 10-man rotation (or) like I’ve said, kind of a fake 11-man rotation ? Where if the first half doesn’t work out, is there someone that you change up?”
 Brazile is at least in the mix for that fake 11th spot if he’s needed this week. Adelman also mentioned Cam Whitmore and rookie Bryce Hopkins, both of whom played with the third unit more than Brazile this preseason.
 “TB has obviously been more of a highlight thing,” Adelman said. “He’s played really well. He also has played the most minutes with the best players. … You can’t be afraid to throw those guys out there as you’re looking for a rotation.”
 Trevon Brazile of the Denver Nuggets poses for a portrait during the team’s media day at Ball Arena in Denver, Colorado on Monday, Sept. 28, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) 
 On the other hand, Denver opens with a Thunder matchup that could make Adelman more hesitant to experiment. The home opener Saturday against New Orleans seems like more fertile ground to introduce players like Brazile.
 If he does get a chance in Oklahoma City, though, he couldn’t pick a much better place to make his debut.
 “Super excited,” he said. “I’m from the Midwest, so I have some family there. Get to have my people go there.”
 Brazile grew up in southwest Missouri and played most of his college career at Arkansas, not far from the Oklahoma border. It’s about a four-hour drive from his hometown to Paycom Center.
 Him even being a candidate to play on opening night didn’t seem like a possibility a week ago. The 23-year-old forward scored 22 points last Wednesday in a preseason loss to the Clippers. Then on Friday, starting in Aaron Gordon’s place against the Lakers, he added 12 efficient points and eight rebounds. The dunks and blocks continued to look enticing.
 Any lingering reluctance from Adelman has more to do with Brazile’s ongoing learning curve — where to space, when to cut, how to read and react to defenses when Denver runs a split action. The second-year coach realizes that playing next to Nikola Jokic is an unusual experience for any rookie.
 “Just don’t anticipate anything,” Brazile said. “There was one play where I anticipated a lob and he threw a bounce pass. So just be ready at all times. He could be looking one way and he’ll throw you the ball, so (I’m) just always having my hands ready.”
 “I thought the Laker game, he spaced much better, as opposed to the Clipper (game and) earlier in the preseason,” Adelman said. “It’s just new for him. … He ran really well, but he’s gotta learn to find the ball earlier offensively. Like, getting on the rim is one thing. Seeing the ball as you do it is another. That attracts people to you. But he did a lot of good things. I’m just happy to see him confidently shoot the ball and look comfortable doing it in a real NBA game.”

 Who do Nuggets need to pop more this season: DeMar DeRozan or Trevon Brazile? 
 That’s been the most tantalizing aspect of Brazile’s performance this month to most of the Nuggets’ higher-ups. His athleticism didn’t need proving. His ability to knock down 3s at his size did. In Denver’s last two preseason games, Brazile shot a 5-for-7 clip from deep, expanding on what he had already showcased at Summer League.
 Still, that doesn’t mean he’s locked up a spot in the rotation. With Spencer Jones returning from a hamstring injury, opportunities inherently will be fewer. Earning trust will take time for the rookie.
 “The best thing about the two draft picks is I’ve yet to see them wonder why they’re being taught something,” Adelman said. “These guys have really bought into everything, playing on a veteran team. That’s really important because you gain respect for the older guys.”
